title: Relative limit criterion for fixed-diagram join boundaries
statement: Use small simplicial sets, quasicategories and coherent functors of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], inner fibrations of [def-coef-infinity-fibrations], and joins and relative limit diagrams of [def-coef-infinity-relative-cone]. Let $q:E\to D$ be an inner fibration of quasicategories, $K$ a small simplicial set, and $c:\Delta^0\star K\to E$ a $q$-limit diagram. For every $d>0$, every map $u:\partial\Delta^d\star K\to E$ whose restriction to $\{d\}\star K$ is $c$, and every map $a:\Delta^d\star K\to D$ with $a|_{\partial\Delta^d\star K}=qu$, there is $\widetilde u:\Delta^d\star K\to E$ with $\widetilde u|_{\partial\Delta^d\star K}=u$ and $q\widetilde u=a$. All equalities are equalities of simplicial maps. No other limit diagrams are assumed, and $K$ may be empty. Equivalently, for $f=c|_K$ let $E_{/f}$ have $k$-simplices the maps $\Delta^k\star K\to E$ restricting to $f$. The functor $E_{/f}\to D_{/qf}$ is an inner fibration, and $c$ is relatively final for it: for every vertex $z$ of $E_{/f}$, the induced map $\operatorname{Map}_{E_{/f}}(z,c)\to\operatorname{Map}_{D_{/qf}}(qz,qc)$ is a weak homotopy equivalence. This uses the fixed-diagram join slice, rather than the internal functor category of cones.

source.place: Definition 4.3.1.1 and Remark 4.3.1.2, printed p. 261, dual limit form in the sharp join slices; Proposition 2.1.2.1 for the slice inner fibration. Applied in Higher Algebra, proof of Theorem 3.1.2.3, step (3), printed p. 341. The comparison to the mapping-space relative-limit definition is the fixed-boundary cone comparison, not an identification of its simplices. Read primary sources online and sandbox PDF copies; shared archive WANTED. No Stacks tag states this infinity-categorical result.

proof.text: Put $f=c|_K$ and $X=E_{/f}$, $Y=D_{/qf}$ in the degreewise model of [lem-coef-infinity-slice-right-fibration]; both are quasicategories. Write $q_f:X\to Y$ for postcomposition. Here is its inner-horn lifting argument. Given a horn $\Lambda_i^n\to X$ over $\Delta^n\to Y$ with $0<i<n$, restrict to the apex blocks and use the inner fibration $q$ to choose $v:\Delta^n\to E$ extending the apex horn over its prescribed base. Glue $v$ to the given $\Lambda_i^n\star K\to E$ along $\Lambda_i^n$. The inclusion $(\Lambda_i^n\star K)\amalg_{\Lambda_i^n}\Delta^n\hookrightarrow\Delta^n\star K$ is inner anodyne by [lem-coef-infinity-anodyne-cocones], with right-anodyne horn $\Lambda_i^n\hookrightarrow\Delta^n$ and monomorphism $\varnothing\hookrightarrow K$. Lift it against $q$ to obtain the desired simplex of $X$. Inner-horn lifting extends to their weakly saturated closure because lifts are preserved by pushouts, successive extensions and retracts. Thus $q_f$ is an inner fibration.

source.place: Proposition 4.3.6.4, applied to an inner horn and the empty-to-K inclusion; Proposition 4.3.6.1 (018F) for the slices.

proof.text:
Let $x=c(*)$ and write $\mu:\Delta_Kx\to f$ for its coherent cone. For an arbitrary vertex $z$ of $X$, write $y=z(*)$ and $\lambda:\Delta_Ky\to f$ for its cone. Apply [lem-coef-join-slice-cocone-comparison] to $K^{\mathrm{op}}\to E^{\mathrm{op}}$ and then take opposites. Order reversal sends $K^{\mathrm{op}}\star\Delta^n$ to $(\Delta^n)^{\mathrm{op}}\star K$; hence the resulting comparison is an equivalence from $X$ to the coherent cone category $(\Delta_K\downarrow f)$, sending $z,c$ to $\lambda,\mu$. The opposite and mapping-space identifications are those of [lem-coef-infinity-relative-cone-equivalence](4). Apply [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus] to this equivalence and the cone-category mapping formula to obtain
$$\operatorname{Map}_X(z,c)\simeq\operatorname{hofib}_{\lambda}\bigl(\operatorname{Map}_E(y,x)\xrightarrow{a\mapsto\mu\Delta_K(a)}\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(K,E)}(\Delta_Ky,f)\bigr).$$
Apply exactly these constructions with $D,qf,q\lambda,q\mu$ to obtain the formula for $\operatorname{Map}_Y(qz,qc)$. The comparison sends a simplex to the coherent cone given by precomposition with the fat-to-sharp join map; that precomposition commutes with postcomposition by $q$. The cone mapping formula is natural in both cones and the ambient functor. Consequently the map between the displayed homotopy fibers is precisely the map on mapping spaces induced by $q_f$, under these natural equivalences.

source.place: Example 4.6.6.8 and Proposition 7.1.6.13 (02XB), proof: the sharp slice/fixed-diagram comparison. The explicit coherent cone mapping formula is supplied by the cited DAG node.

proof.text:
By the limit clause of [lem-coef-infinity-relative-cone-constant-test], the hypothesis that $c$ is a $q$-limit makes the square with rows
$$A=\operatorname{Map}_E(y,x)\longrightarrow B=\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(K,E)}(\Delta_Ky,f),\qquad C=\operatorname{Map}_D(qy,qx)\longrightarrow H=\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(K,D)}(\Delta_K(qy),qf)$$
a homotopy pullback, with horizontal maps induced by $\mu,q\mu$ and vertical maps induced by $q$. In particular $A\simeq B\times_H^h C$. Pull back this comparison homotopically along the vertex $\lambda:\Delta^0\to B$. Homotopy-pullback invariance and pasting, [lem-coef-kan-homotopy-pullback-invariance] and [lem-coef-infinity-homotopy-pullback-pasting], give
$$\operatorname{hofib}_{\lambda}(A\to B)\simeq\{\lambda\}\times_B^h(B\times_H^h C)\simeq\{q\lambda\}\times_H^h C=\operatorname{hofib}_{q\lambda}(C\to H).$$
All pullbacks here use path spaces and the commutation homotopy of the constant-test square, including its higher simplices. Step 2 identifies this fiber comparison with $\operatorname{Map}_X(z,c)\to\operatorname{Map}_Y(qz,qc)$. As $z$ was arbitrary, $c$ is $q_f$-final.

source.place: Proposition 7.1.6.19, constant-source characterization of relative limits, followed by the homotopy-fiber calculation. The cited DAG constant-test node gives the apex mapping-space version.

proof.text: Apply the final-object clause of [lem-coef-infinity-relative-initial-boundary] to $q_f:X\to Y$, which is an inner fibration by step 1, and its $q_f$-final vertex $c$ from step 3. For every $d>0$, every $b:\partial\Delta^d\to X$ with $b(d)=c$ and every $a':\Delta^d\to Y$ restricting to $q_fb$ admit a filler $w:\Delta^d\to X$ with $w|_{\partial\Delta^d}=b$ and $q_fw=a'$. The same cited criterion proves that this boundary-filling assertion is equivalent to the mapping-space relative-finality assertion, explaining the equivalence in the item.

source.place: Corollary 7.1.5.17, conditions (1) and (3), in the opposite final-object orientation.

proof.text: To translate the preceding lifting problem, for each simplex $s:\Delta^n\to\partial\Delta^d$ define $b(s)=u\circ(s\star\operatorname{id}_K)$. Its restriction on $K$ is $f$ because $K\subseteq\{d\}\star K$ and $u|_{\{d\}\star K}=c$. On a simplicial operator $\alpha$ this formula gives $b(s\alpha)=b(s)\circ(\Delta(\alpha)\star\operatorname{id}_K)$, so it defines the required simplicial map $b$ into $X$. The identical formula for $a$ gives $a':\Delta^d\to Y$, with $q_fb=a'|_{\partial\Delta^d}$ and $b(d)=c$. Conversely compatible maps on the joined simplices glue to a map on the join: by the degreewise join formula, every mixed simplex has one initial simplex of the first factor and one final simplex of $K$, and their faces restrict these blocks. Uncurrying $w$ therefore gives $\widetilde u:\Delta^d\star K\to E$. On each boundary simplex it agrees with $u$, and on every simplex its composite with $q$ is $a$, proving both exact equations. Currying reverses this construction. For $K=\varnothing$, the join degree formula gives $L\star\varnothing=L$ and $X=E,Y=D$, so these formulas reduce to the same boundary problem with no extra data. For $d=1$ the final vertex is still present in the boundary; dimension zero is neither used nor asserted.
